en: Itivuttaka 21:
Ekakanipāta,
Third Chapter (Tatiyavagga)
The Discourse on the Serene Mind.
This was said by the Blessed One; thus have I heard:
"In this case, monks, having encompassed with my own mind the mind of a certain person whose mind is serene, I understand it thus: [he will be reborn in a certain state]."
"And if this person were to pass away at this very moment, they would be placed in heaven as if carried there.
For what reason?
Because, monks, their mind is serene.
“Monks, it is because of mental clarity that some beings, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world.
Thus the Blessed One spoke. With regard to this, it is said:
“Having recognized that a certain person here has a mind of confidence,
he explained this matter.”
In the presence of the monks,
at this very moment,
a person might pass away.
One would be reborn in a happy destination,
for one's mind has been made serene;
as if having carried [something] there, one were to deposit it.
In this very way,
such beings go to a happy destination because of their serenity of mind.
This matter too was spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
First.
